title: Cochain bounds and full embeddings for finite filtered localizations
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration]. A uniformly finite decreasing filtered cochain complex $K$ has subcomplexes $F^pK$ with $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, independent of cochain degree; put $\operatorname{gr}^pK=F^pK/F^{p+1}K$. Let $DF(\mathcal A)$ be the localization of these complexes at chain maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every grade. Let $D^bF(\mathcal A)$, $D^+F(\mathcal A)$ and $D^-F(\mathcal A)$ be the analogous localizations of complexes bounded, bounded below and bounded above in cochain degree, respectively. The natural functors from each of these three categories into $DF(\mathcal A)$ are fully faithful. Their essential images consist respectively of objects whose graded cohomology vanishes outside a common finite cochain interval, below a common cochain bound, and above a common cochain bound. Consequently $D^bF(\mathcal A)\to D^+F(\mathcal A)$ and $D^bF(\mathcal A)\to D^-F(\mathcal A)$ are fully faithful. All these assertions restrict to any fixed filtration interval $[a,b]$. The required bounded representatives can be obtained by good cochain truncations with induced subobject/quotient filtrations: if $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$ for all $p$ and $n<c$, the map $K\to\tau^{\ge c}K$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism; dually if all graded cohomology vanishes above $d$, then $\tau^{\le d}K\to K$ is one. These truncations change only the cutoff term and the cochain degrees beyond it and do not enlarge $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tags 05S6 (lemma-filtered-bounded-derived) and 05S5 (lemma-filtered-complex-cohomology-bounded), with definition-filtered-derived-bounded. Restrict to a fixed filtration interval; their truncation and roof arguments preserve that interval.

proof.text:
Suppose all graded cohomology below $c$ vanishes. Apply [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness] to $K^{c-2}\to K^{c-1}\to K^c$: its graded sequence is exact at the middle because $H^{c-1}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$. In particular $v=d^{c-1}$ is strict, so, writing $I=\operatorname{im}v$, we have $I\cap F^pK^c=v(F^pK^{c-1})$. Use the good truncation of [def-kun-truncations], with quotient filtration on its degree-$c$ term $K^c/I$ and the original filtration above $c$. The quotient formula gives
$$\operatorname{gr}^p(K^c/I)=F^pK^c/(F^{p+1}K^c+(I\cap F^pK^c))=\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{gr}^pv).$$
Here the first equality denotes the canonical quotient isomorphism, and the second follows from strictness. Thus $\operatorname{gr}^p(\tau^{\ge c}K)=\tau^{\ge c}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$, including the induced differential at the cutoff. The cohomology formula for good truncation in [def-kun-truncations] shows that $K\to\tau^{\ge c}K$ induces an isomorphism on every graded cohomology object: it retains degrees $n\ge c$, while the removed cohomology was zero. Only degrees at most $c$ change, and induced quotient filtrations preserve $F^a=K$, $F^{b+1}=0$.

source.place: Tag 05S5, lemma-filtered-complex-cohomology-bounded (1); Homology Tag 05QH, lemma-filtered-acyclic, and the quotient computation in Tag 0127, lemma-characterize-strict.

proof.text:
Suppose all graded cohomology above $d$ vanishes. Apply [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness] to $K^d\to K^{d+1}\to K^{d+2}$, using exactness at degree $d+1$. It makes $v=d^d$ strict. Set $Z=\ker v$, filtered by $Z\cap F^pK^d$, and take the good truncation $\tau^{\le d}K$ of [def-kun-truncations]. Strictness gives the subobject identity
$$F^pK^d\cap v^{-1}(F^{p+1}K^{d+1})=(Z\cap F^pK^d)+F^{p+1}K^d.$$
Indeed the images of the two sides under $v$ are both $v(F^pK^d)\cap F^{p+1}K^{d+1}=v(F^{p+1}K^d)$, and both contain the kernel $Z\cap F^pK^d$. Taking the quotient by $F^{p+1}K^d$ identifies the kernel of $\operatorname{gr}^pv$ with $(Z\cap F^pK^d)/(Z\cap F^{p+1}K^d)=\operatorname{gr}^pZ$. Therefore $\operatorname{gr}^p(\tau^{\le d}K)=\tau^{\le d}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$, with its induced incoming differential. Good truncation retains cohomology in degrees $n\le d$ and discards only the vanishing cohomology above $d$, so $\tau^{\le d}K\to K$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism. Its induced subobject filtration preserves $[a,b]$ and only degrees at least $d$ change.

source.place: Tag 05S5, lemma-filtered-complex-cohomology-bounded (2), the dual cutoff argument; Homology Tag 05QH, lemma-filtered-acyclic.

proof.text: Every functor $H^n\operatorname{gr}^p$ inverts graded quasi-isomorphisms by their definition, so the universal property of localization makes graded cohomology invariant under isomorphisms in $DF(\mathcal A)$. A cochain-bounded representative has the corresponding common cohomology bounds, independent of $p$. Conversely steps 1 and 2 give the one-sided representatives. If cohomology is supported in $[c,d]$, choose $c\le d$ (in the entirely acyclic case any such pair works), put $L=\tau^{\ge c}K$, and put $N=\tau^{\le d}L$. Then $K\to L\leftarrow N$ consists of graded quasi-isomorphisms and $N$ is zero outside $[c,d]$. The second truncation leaves the zero terms below $c$ zero. This proves each asserted essential-image description once full faithfulness is established.

We may calculate the stated chain-map localizations using filtered chain maps modulo filtered homotopy. Here is the universal-property check, without assuming that finite filtered objects form an abelian category. Given $f-g=dh+hd$, use $\operatorname{Cyl}(K)=K\oplus C(1_K)$ with the direct-sum filtration. In degree $n$ its coordinates $(x,y,z)$ belong to $K^n\oplus K^n\oplus K^{n+1}$ and its differential is $(dx,dy+z,-dz)$. The projection $\pi(x,y,z)=x$ has sections $j_0(x)=(x,0,0)$ and $j_1(x)=(x,x,0)$. On $C(1_K)$ the degree-$-1$ map $(y,z)\mapsto(0,y)$ satisfies $dH+Hd=1$ on every grade. Thus $\pi$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism. The formula $t^n(x,y,z)=g^nx+(f^n-g^n)y+h^{n+1}z$ defines a chain map, since $f-g=dh+hd$, and $tj_0=g$, $tj_1=f$. Every functor inverting graded quasi-isomorphisms therefore identifies $f$ and $g$, because it identifies both sections with $\pi^{-1}$. It factors uniquely through the homotopy category. Applying the universal property again after localization gives the claimed equivalence of the two localization models. These cylinder formulas preserve uniform filtration bounds and each of the three kinds of cochain boundedness.

source.place: Section filtered-derived-category, Tag 05S2, definition-filtered-derived; explicit cylinder verification, using the direct-sum contractible cone of lemma-make-injective.

proof.text: Construct the dg category of uniformly finite filtered cochain complexes: degree-$r$ maps are $\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_F(K^n,L^{n+r})$, with $\partial h=d_Lh-(-1)^rh d_K$ and ordinary graded composition. The equations $d_K^2=d_L^2=0$ give $\partial^2=0$ and the Leibniz rule. Closed degree-zero maps are filtered chain maps, and boundaries are precisely filtered null homotopies. Enlarge universes to make this dg category small. The zero complex and finite direct sums give axiom (A) of [lem-coef-dg-abc-homotopy-category-triangulated]. For (B), set $(K[m])^n=K^{n+m}$, $d_{K[m]}=(-1)^m d_K$, and $h[m]^n=(-1)^{mr}h^{n+m}$ on degree-$r$ maps. These formulas commute with $\partial$, satisfy $[m][l]=[m+l]$, and identify $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K,L[m])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K,L)[m]$. For (C), take $C(f)^n=L^n\oplus K^{n+1}$ with differential $(d_Ly+fx,-d_Kx)$ and the direct-sum filtration. The coordinate inclusion and projection of $L\to C(f)\to K[1]$ have the graded splittings required in the cited statement; the splitting boundary is $f[1]$. Consequently its conclusion gives the filtered homotopy category its cone triangulation. All these formulas use finite sums and shifts, so they apply separately to the bounded, bounded-below and bounded-above dg subcategories and to every fixed filtration interval.

source.place: Tags 09QJ, situation-ABC, and 09QY, proposition-ABC-homotopy-category-triangulated; explicit dg category of filtered complexes.

proof.text: In any of the homotopy categories in step 5 let $\mathcal S$ be the full replete subcategory of objects with all grades acyclic. The grade of a shifted complex or a cone is the corresponding shift or cone of its grade, since the cone filtration is a direct sum. Hence every cone triangle maps to a distinguished triangle of the ordinary derived category as defined in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] makes $\mathcal S$ closed under shifts and triangles: with two graded cohomology sequences identically zero, exactness forces the third to be zero. It contains zero and is additive. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], a map has cone in $\mathcal S$ exactly when it is a graded quasi-isomorphism. Thus [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] supplies both calculi of fractions for precisely the required maps, in every one of these homotopy categories. Their class also satisfies two-out-of-three directly, by applying every $H^n\operatorname{gr}^p$ and using two-out-of-three for isomorphisms. We can now use roofs and their common refinements without any injective or projective hypothesis on $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 05S1, lemma-filtered-acyclic, via Tag 05RG, lemma-construct-multiplicative-system; graded cones and long exact cohomology.

proof.text: For fullness of $D^+F\to DF$, take bounded-below $K,L$. By [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-representation] an ambient morphism is represented in the filtered homotopy category by $K\xrightarrow f Z\xleftarrow s L$, with $s$ a graded quasi-isomorphism. Since $L$ is cochain-bounded below, there is a common lower bound $c$ on all $H^n\operatorname{gr}^pZ$, inherited through $s$. Step 1 provides $q:Z\to\tau^{\ge c}Z$ in the same class. Postcompose the roof with $q$. Its middle object is bounded below and $(qf,qs)$ represents the same ambient morphism, proving surjectivity on Hom sets.

source.place: Tag 05S6, lemma-filtered-bounded-derived (1), following the fullness paragraph of Tag 05RW, lemma-bounded-derived.

proof.text: For faithfulness take two roofs $(f_i:K\to Z_i,s_i:L\to Z_i)$ in the bounded-below homotopy category which become equal in $DF$. The statement of [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-equality] gives maps $t_i:Z_i\to T$ with $t_1s_1=t_2s_2$ in the graded quasi-isomorphisms and $t_1f_1=t_2f_2$. The common denominator identifies every graded cohomology object of $T$ with that of $L$, so it has a common lower bound $c$. Postcompose both equalities with the graded quasi-isomorphism $T\to\tau^{\ge c}T$ of step 1. Now the two comparison maps and their common denominator lie in the bounded-below homotopy category, where the same cited equality criterion proves that the original roofs were equal already. This proves injectivity on Hom sets and hence full faithfulness of $D^+F\to DF$.

source.place: Tag 05S6 (1); faithfulness argument of Tag 05RW, lemma-bounded-derived, with common refinements instead of subtraction.

proof.text: For $D^-F\to DF$ use the right roofs of [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation]. If $K,L$ are bounded above, an ambient morphism has a roof $K\xleftarrow s Z\xrightarrow f L$, $s$ a graded quasi-isomorphism. A cochain upper bound for $K$ is a common graded cohomology upper bound $d$ for $Z$. Precompose with $q:\tau^{\le d}Z\to Z$ from step 2; the roof $(sq,fq)$ now has bounded-above middle object. For faithfulness, [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] says that two equal ambient roofs admit $a_i:T\to Z_i$ with $s_1a_1=s_2a_2$ a graded quasi-isomorphism and $f_1a_1=f_2a_2$. Their common denominator gives a common upper cohomology bound $d$ for $T$. Precompose both equalities with $\tau^{\le d}T\to T$. This is a common refinement inside the bounded-above homotopy category, so the same equality criterion proves equality there. Thus the functor is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 05S6 (2), dual to the proof of Tag 05RW, lemma-bounded-derived (1).

proof.text: To prove $D^bF\to D^-F$ fully faithful, repeat steps 7 and 8 with bounded $K,L$ and ambient category the bounded-above homotopy category. The left-fraction representation and equality statements still apply by step 6. Every middle object $Z$, and every equality witness $T$, already has some cochain upper bound. Applying $\tau^{\ge c}$ to it as in steps 7 and 8 retains that upper bound while imposing the lower bound, and hence gives a bounded middle object or bounded equality witness. This proves both fullness and faithfulness, using [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-representation] and [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-equality]. Compose with step 9 to obtain full faithfulness of $D^bF\to DF$. Finally the inclusion $D^bF\to D^+F$, followed by the fully faithful $D^+F\to DF$, is this fully faithful functor. On Hom sets the second map and the composite are bijections, so the first map is a bijection too. This proves both asserted intermediate inclusions.

source.place: Tag 05S6 (3), following the last paragraph of the proof of Tag 05RW, lemma-bounded-derived.

proof.text: Fix any filtration interval $[a,b]$ at the outset. In steps 1 and 2 the cutoff terms have the induced quotient and subobject filtrations of [def-sp-filtration], so $F^a$ is still the whole term and $F^{b+1}$ is still zero. The dg sums, shifts, cone splittings and cylinder in steps 4 and 5 also retain these exact two bounds. Consequently step 6 gives fractions in the homotopy categories with this fixed interval, and every roof replacement and equality refinement in steps 7–10 remains in those same categories. The bounded representatives in step 3 do too. Thus the entire proof, including all three essential-image characterizations and both intermediate inclusions, holds for the fixed-interval localizations themselves; it does not infer this by asserting that they are full subcategories of a larger localization.
